title: Which lighting statements does the graph really support?
description: A line graph shows the main source of lighting, kerosene or electricity, in rural and urban homes over the years. The video checks four statements against the right line and the right year, and finds the one the graph cannot support at all.
teaching_notes: One idea: a statement is valid only if the right line, read at the right year, supports it, and a graph says nothing about what it does not measure. Watch for students who accept a statement because it sounds true.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 10)
video_script.why: The child has read what a graph shows and what it leaves out, and now judges four statements about it.
video_script.substitution: For each statement, find the right line and the right year, read the value, and ask whether the graph measures what the statement claims.
video_script.anchor: the book's line graph of the primary source of lighting in rural and urban homes
video_script.payoff_line: statements three and four are not supported by the graph

final_answer.value: Statements (iii) and (iv) are not supported by the graph; (i) and (ii) are checked against the lines
final_answer.spoken: statements three and four are not supported by the graph, and statements one and two are checked against the lines

never_show: a statement that is accepted without reading the line
maths_rules: graph: kerosene and electricity as the primary lighting source, rural and urban, over the years from 1983 to 2023
(i) valid if in 1983 the rural kerosene line is above half and the urban electricity line is above half
(ii) valid if both kerosene lines slope down over the years
(iii) the urban electricity line in 2000 is far above 10 percent, so the statement is not valid
(iv) the graph shows the main source of lighting, not power cuts, so it cannot support the statement
slip: a statement can sound true and still not be supported by the graph
video_script.design: One idea: check each statement against the right line and year, and against what the graph measures. The graph stays on screen all video; each statement gets a tick or a cross only in the answer beat.
open_questions: The graph values are not in the extracted book text, so the verdicts on (i) and (ii) depend on the lines in the figure; the worklist asks for them to be checked against the lines.
